content.text: ➀ syndesmotic ligament (connects tibia & fibula in the lower leg)
▪︎lat MC (plantar-flexed foot inverted) - medial & high sprains more severe
: pain · swelling · ecchymosis · limited ROM · ↑joint laxity · impaired or unable to bear wt
Grade II: lrger but incomplete tear
▪︎Grade I: mild swelling/tenderness · ⍉instability · bears wt w minimal pain
▪︎Grade II: mod pain · swelling & ecchymosis · mod instability · pain w wt bearing
▪︎Grade III: severe pain · swelling & ecchymosis · unable to bear wt · sig instability
▪︎squeeze test: pain near anterior tibiofibular ligament → syndesmotic sprain
▪︎external rotation test: pain anterior to lat malleolus prox to joint
*anterior drawer & talar tilt more reliable for chronic instability (spasm/swelling → false ⊖ acutely) - compare to unaffected side
ddx navicular stress frx: gradual vague dorsal midfoot pain w workouts · exquisite navicular TTP
ddx 5th metatarsal shaft frx: exquisite TTP · ecchymosis · edema @ 5th metatarsal
ddx osteochondral lesion: effusion · joint tenderness · dull pain since prior ankle inj
Exam: pulses · ecchymosis · deformity · ROM - palpate both malleoli · entire tibia & fibula (incl fibular head) · 5th metatarsal base · midfoot · hindfoot · calcaneus · Achilles
▪︎stress test ligaments only after frx excluded (imaging or Ottawa)
Ottawa ankle rules (w.in 48h of inj · >5yo): XR if tenderness @ posterior edge of distal 6cm or tip of lat or medial malleolus · or unable to bear wt 4 steps immediately & @ eval
▪︎foot XR: tender 5th metatarsal base · navicular · or unable to bear wt 4 steps
▪︎~100% sens for malleolar frx - ⍉use if intoxicated · AMS · baseline LE neuro deficit
▪︎Maisonneuve: prox fibula frx w medial ankle disrupt
▪︎grade II: LE splint or walking boot
: ⍉resolution w conservative · severe grade III lat sprains · deltoid disrupt · ↑ankle sprain · chronic ankle instability
▪︎RICE (lacking formal studies) · funct bracing · funct rehab
▪︎emerging: MEAT (movement · exercise · analgesia · treatment) · MOVE (movement · options · vary · ease)
: posterior tibial n. compress as it travels thru tarsal tunnel (ie, flexor retinaculum of foot) below medial malleolus
pain/numbness @ medial malleolus · heel · sole & first 3 toes
: pain reproduced by tapping tarsal tunnel
